articles.title: Global investors slash dollar-hedging ratio to lowest since 2014
articles.excerpt:
Global investors in US stocks and bonds dropped protection against dollar declines to the lowest since 2014 as expected monetary-policy tightening from the Federal Reserve makes hedging more costly, according to State Street Corp.

The Fed left interest rates unchanged this week, but traders are betting the central bank will hike as soon as December and again in 2027. Those wagers drew support from Chairman Kevin Warsh’s press conference this week, when he cited a strong economy and warned over persistent inflation.

articles.title: Boris Vujčić: Integrated, open and resilient: Europe’s strengths in a fragmenting world
articles.excerpt:
Thank you to the Central Bank of Ireland for organising this conference and inviting me to speak. It is a great pleasure to be here in Dublin. Ireland illustrates why the topics of today’s event – from geopolitics to financial resilience – are timely.

Ireland has one of the most open economies in the world and it is deeply integrated into European and global markets. It is a Single Market success story, and a reminder that openness remains one of Europe’s greatest strengths.

But openness works both ways. A shift in US trade policy or a turn in global capital flows can spill over to the Irish economy particularly quickly.
